payload.name: Preserve explicit facts during candidate extraction and CRUD
payload.description: When a user message states multiple distinct facts, especially activities plus objects, accessories, or answers to direct questions, use separate extraction candidates and verify none are dropped before UPDATE or MERGE.
content: During extraction, when a single user message states multiple distinct explicit facts, do not consolidate them into one activity-focused summary. Create separate candidates for facts about objects, accessories, clothing, preferences, or answers to direct questions, ensuring every explicit claim appears in at least one candidate.

Before applying an UPDATE, MERGE, or ADD, re-check the candidate against its source messages; if an explicit fact is missing, add it to the candidate or create an additional candidate rather than letting it be dropped.
When a fact does not fit an existing memory's dominant theme, record it as its own ADD candidate instead of omitting it or forcing it into an unrelated enrichment.

solves: Diagnosed cause: extraction collapsed a multi-fact message into one activity summary, omitting an explicit object/accessory fact that later questions rely on. The reusable failure is incomplete candidate coverage when a message mixes activities with separate objects, preferences, or answers to direct questions. The rule requires every explicit claim to survive in some candidate, using separate ADD candidates when facts do not share the dominant theme. It applies to any future extraction/CRUD session with multi-fact user messages; it does not apply to inferring facts the user never stated.
